summary: Four PM agents in parallel propose v0.5/v1.0/v2.0 wave sequencing; Release Captain synthesizes

v0_5_targets: hashkit: Implement real PDQ via the pdqhash Apache-2.0 crate so hash_from_luma returns a PdqResult byte-identical to upstream generate_pdq on the same luma buffer, and hash_dihedral_from_luma returns 8 distinct dihedral hashes; cargo test --workspace --all-features green plus a demo that hashes a 256x256 luma buffer and prints the 64-hex hash.

hashkit: Stand up vectors/v0/corpus.json as the versioned conformance artifact and prove byte-identical hashes against the facebook/ThreatExchange C++ PDQ reference on at least 20 synthetic inputs, with CI failing closed on any corpus drift.

hashkit-match: Implement PdqMatcher::query and query_all as a naive linear scan that matches ground truth on a 1,000-hash synthetic corpus over 100 random queries, with the DEFAULT_HAMMING_THRESHOLD=31 contract documented and tested; no network, dry-run only.

detectkit-test: Implement deterministic generate_image for at least 5 patterns (gradient-horizontal/vertical/radial, checkerboard, structured-noise) so identical (identifier, seed, pattern, width, height) yields byte-identical PNG output verified by SHA-256, plus a generate_corpus that emits a small corpus + manifest.

detectkit-test: Wire the generated images through hashkit to populate the expected PDQ hashes in packages/hashkit/vectors/v0/corpus.json and make the verify subcommand re-run the corpus and confirm zero drift in dry-run.

All three: Land README examples, a tiny runnable demo per package, and failure-mode tests (empty/oversized luma, zero-provider matcher refusal, unknown-pattern error), and pass bash scripts/safety-check.sh proving synthetic-only fixtures and no credential dependency.
v1_0_targets: hashkit: Make hash outputs reproducible across native and WASM builds — wasm-pack build produces byte-identical hashes to the native Rust build on the full v0 corpus in CI — then freeze the public PDQ API (PdqHash/PdqQuality/PdqResult/PdqError) under semver with a documented stability/deprecation policy and publish hashkit 0.1.0 to crates.io and npm.

hashkit: Promote the versioned synthetic corpus to the canonical conformance artifact that downstream package tests consume, with the spec/algorithm version pinned so consumers (csam-shield, hashstream, trainguard) can lock a known-good hash version.

hashkit-match: Validate match behavior against linear-scan ground truth at scale (closest-within-threshold and ordered query_all matching naive over 100 randomized queries against 10,000-hash reference sets), freeze the matcher API and threshold contract under semver, document false-positive handling / human-review escalation as the required downstream step, and publish hashkit-match 0.1.0.

detectkit-test: Version the synthetic corpus as a consumable test artifact other tracks depend on, expand patterns and add perceptual-robustness fixtures (rotation/scale/crop/recompression) and malformed/empty-input cases, ship the verify drift-check as a reusable gate, and publish detectkit-test 0.1.0 to PyPI.

All three: Meet the program v1.0 gate — every package has README examples, changelog, license metadata, and a STATUS line; CI covers the Rust workspace and the Python package; and docs/roadmap.md matches the package STATUS files.
v2_0_targets: hashkit: Add the multi-index Hamming-adjacent performance work and additional vetted algorithms where in scope (TMK video features_from_frames as the second algorithm, keeping the slow reference path as the conformance oracle), and add fuzzing over the decode/normalize pipeline; the pdqhash-backed path remains the byte-identical oracle.

hashkit: Run a continuous cross-platform conformance matrix in CI (macOS, Linux, Windows for the Rust core plus WASM) with mandatory corpus-drift gates that block any release introducing a hash mismatch, and sign release artifacts (crates/npm) via Sigstore/cosign.

hashkit-match: Ship the real Multi-Index Hashing (MIH) implementation that matches naive ground truth and benchmarks faster than linear scan at >=10,000-hash sets (the whole point of the algorithm), scale to large operator blocklists with bounded-latency queries, and add audit-logging / result-provenance fields for operator accountability and downstream report/escalation handoff.

detectkit-test: Operate as the portfolio-wide conformance authority — corpus drift checks mandatory in CI for every PDQ-dependent tool, an adversarial/robustness corpus (perturbation attacks against perceptual hashing), and a certification workflow where a downstream tool declares spec version + binding, runs the suite, and gets a machine-checkable conformance report.

All three: External contributors can reproduce conformance on macOS, Linux, and Windows (independent WASM-build reproduction by an outside contributor is the documented Beta-honesty bar), release artifacts are signed, and a supported-version + spec-evolution governance policy is published.
can_ship_no_externals: hashkit PDQ implementation via the pdqhash Apache-2.0 crate (hash_from_luma + hash_dihedral_from_luma) — pure compute, no network, no credentials.
The versioned vectors/v0/corpus.json conformance artifact validated against the public facebook/ThreatExchange C++ PDQ reference, with CI corpus-drift gating.
hashkit-match naive linear-scan query/query_all and the documented Hamming-threshold (31) contract, driven entirely by synthetic hashes.
detectkit-test deterministic generate_image (>=5 patterns), generate_corpus, and the verify drift-check — synthetic non-CSAM media only.
The detectkit-test -> hashkit corpus-population loop that records expected PDQ hashes for the synthetic corpus.
Native-vs-WASM byte-identical reproducibility proof in CI (the v1.0 reproducibility bar) and registry publication of all three at 0.1.0.
The 'no real CSAM hashes, no real credentials, synthetic fixtures only' safety invariant enforced via bash scripts/safety-check.sh.

cross_track_deps.needs: NCMEC-verified hash vectors to add a credentialed subset (ncmec_verified: true) to vectors/v0/corpus.json
cross_track_deps.why: This is the hashkit BETA-promotion bar (>=50 verified vectors), NOT a v0.5/v1.0 blocker. v0.5 and v1.0 ship entirely on synthetic vectors against the public C++ reference; only post-1.0 Beta hardening needs the credential chain (gated behind the Lantern ESP outreach in docs/sponsorship.md).

cross_track_deps.needs: Their required hashkit version pin and the match-result/MatchResponse schema expectations they will consume
cross_track_deps.why: Foundation must freeze the PDQ API, on-disk hash encoding, and matcher result shape under semver at v1.0 before downstream can build a safe production integration surface; a late schema change would break every PDQ-dependent tool.

cross_track_deps.needs: Confirmation that publicly distributing the synthetic detectkit-test corpus and the derived PDQ hash vectors raises no legal/safety concern
cross_track_deps.why: detectkit-test is the public test artifact the whole portfolio conforms to; counsel/captain sign-off that synthetic-only fixtures are safe to publish protects the no-real-CSAM invariant before we tag releases.

blockers: Internal cross-package ordering (not a true external blocker, but the critical path): detectkit-test cannot record expected hashes in vectors/v0/corpus.json until hashkit's PDQ port produces working hashes. The roadmap states they advance together — hashkit's reference impl must land before detectkit-test can close its corpus loop and before hashkit-match has real hashes to match.

Byte-identical native-vs-WASM reproducibility (the v1.0 bar) can be threatened by floating-point / decode nondeterminism in the PDQ pipeline; if the pdqhash crate or its image decode path is not deterministic across the native and wasm32 targets, achieving byte-identical output may require pinning decoders or an integer/fixed-point path. Needs early validation in v0.5, not discovery at v1.0.

NCMEC ESP credentialing (Lantern outreach, docs/sponsorship.md) gates only the Beta-tier credentialed corpus subset and is explicitly NOT a v0.5/v1.0 blocker — flagged here so the Council does not mistakenly treat the foundation track as credential-blocked.

Legal/safety confirmation that the synthetic corpus and derived hash vectors are safe to publish publicly is a non-code sign-off the Foundation PM cannot grant alone; it sits with the Release Captain / Legal-Ops seat.
order_of_attack: 1. hashkit PDQ first (hash_from_luma + hash_dihedral_from_luma via the pdqhash crate). It is the root of the dependency tree — hashkit-match, detectkit-test's corpus loop, and all of Wave 2-3 PDQ work are blocked until real hashes exist. Depth-first conformance here outranks everything.

2. In parallel-but-slightly-behind, build detectkit-test's deterministic generate_image and generators so synthetic inputs are ready the moment hashkit can hash them; this keeps the two on their documented 'advance together' track.

3. Close the corpus loop: run detectkit-test images through hashkit, populate vectors/v0/corpus.json, and prove byte-identical output against the facebook/ThreatExchange C++ PDQ reference with CI drift-gating. This conformance proof is the foundation everyone downstream trusts.

4. hashkit-match naive linear-scan query/query_all validated against ground truth on a 1,000-hash synthetic set (defer MIH to v2.0 per the execution plan — naive is acceptable through v1.0). Matching is meaningless until the hashes underneath are byte-stable, so this comes after the corpus is proven.

5. Prove native-vs-WASM byte-identical reproducibility in CI — the v1.0 gate that makes cross-platform downstream trust possible — then freeze the PDQ + matcher APIs under semver and publish all three at 0.1.0.

6. Only after v0.5/v1.0 are solid: harden for v2.0 — real MIH with benchmarks, TMK video as the second algorithm, the cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows) conformance matrix, adversarial/robustness corpus, signed artifacts, and the certification workflow.

v0_5_targets: csam-shield: Ship a one-command local demo (`npm run demo` / `make demo`) that runs the existing `createShield` engine with the bundled mock/custom detector against detectkit-test synthetic fixtures, returning the normalized {verdict: match|nomatch|pending, matchType, confidence, providers[], hashes} envelope and writing a JSONL AuditSink record (hashes + verdict + timestamp, never image bytes). Default-deny on uncertainty: near-match -> pending/review handoff, never auto-block or auto-report.

csam-shield: Document the stub-detector-by-default posture and the operator-supplied real-provider boundary (Arachnid Shield free self-serve key, self-hosted PDQ/Open Media Match, Cloudflare, PhotoDNA), plus the explicit non-goals: the NCMEC Reporter stays a stub wiring point requiring the operator's own ESP credentials and counsel sign-off.

csam-shield: Failure-mode tests for the dry-run path — timeout containment, audit-sink failure isolation, empty-detector-list rejection (extending the existing 6 Node / 7 Python tests) — demonstrating fail-safe behavior with fake detectors only.

promptshield: Promote the already-implemented Stage 1 conjunction-principle matcher to a usable dry-run `guard(prompt, negative_prompt=None) -> Verdict{allow|block|review, score, matched_signals, policy_version}` plus `score`/`screen` CLI, content-free (SHA-256-of-normalized-prompt audit only), CPU-only, no model download. Uncertain -> review (default-deny: ambiguous never silently allowed).

promptshield: Ship a runnable local demo over a bundled benign + obviously-unsafe + ambiguous prompt corpus showing allow/block/review routing, with negative-prompt evasion handling (e.g. 'adult'/'mature' stuffed in negatives) exercised, so an operator can eyeball the safety bias before wiring it in.

c2pa-lite: Ship a one-command `c2pa-lite` sign->verify round-trip on a sample PNG/JPEG using a local PKCS#8 dev key (the placeholder signature path that round-trips in tests today), emitting the normalized verify JSON {signed? trusted-issuer? watermark-decoded? recovered-from-store?} with dev-key signatures clearly labeled untrusted. Watermark embed/extract remain documented-NotImplemented.

c2pa-lite: Document the supported manifest claim subset (claim_id, producer, ai_generated, generator, metadata pairs) and the dev test-anchor trust list, and state the non-goal loudly: c2pa-lite marks provenance and does NOT detect or hash CSAM.

All three: A uniform `make demo` / documented one-command entrypoint per package that installs, runs the dry-run flow against bundled synthetic fixtures, and exits 0 — the afternoon-adoption acceptance test — passing `bash scripts/safety-check.sh`.
v1_0_targets: csam-shield: Wire at least one real low-friction detector behind the existing adapter interface as an operator-supplied, env-gated path — Arachnid Shield (free self-serve key) and/or self-hosted PDQ via hashkit+hashkit-match — with a published Express + Fastify + FastAPI + Hono example each, while the stub/mock detector stays the zero-config default.

csam-shield: Production-grade resilience controls — retry, timeout, circuit-breaker/fallback when an upstream is down, and explicit fail-closed/fail-open policy knobs (the value-add over rolling your own) — with the queue-backed pending flow (in-memory default, BullMQ/SQS adapter seam) and a stable semver-versioned `MatchResponse`.

csam-shield: Documented operator responsibilities — human-in-the-loop on near matches, no auto-report/auto-ban, signed audit-event schema, and the NCMEC Reporter hand-off contract (still a wiring point to the Legal/Ops track, not built-in reporting).

promptshield: Ship the Stage 2 ONNX classifier trained on a synthetic/red-team corpus (zero real CSAM), with a published precision/recall + false-positive-rate report on a benign holdout and >=90% recall on a public adversarial set, plus an adversarial jailbreak regression suite (homoglyphs, token-splitting, euphemism rotation, multilingual, prompt-injection) gating CI so the deny posture can't silently weaken.

promptshield: Stable `guard()` API + operator config surface (threshold tuning, allow/block/review routing) with safe defaults locked to default-deny, model+lexicon as versioned Hugging Face artifacts (policy updates without code changes), and documented adapter tests for diffusers/vLLM/ComfyUI without requiring model downloads by default.

c2pa-lite: Land the `upstream` feature path so signing delegates to c2pa-rs for real C2PA manifests, verifiable by the official c2patool and wire-compatible with Adobe/CAI Verify; production signing via KMS/PKCS#11 with a documented trust anchor, and correct trusted-vs-untrusted result semantics in a stable verify API suitable for an ingestion/moderation pipeline.

c2pa-lite: Documented interop conformance against c2patool/CAI Verify for the supported manifest subset, with the watermark soft-binding slot kept behind a clearly-flagged experimental boundary (no robustness claims until a scheme stabilizes).

All three: semver-stable public APIs; per-package SECURITY.md + README security checklist; threat-model note covering the abuse surface (detector evasion, false-allow on uncertain, false-sense-of-security from a 'certified' badge) — the credibility floor for production adoption of CSAM-adjacent tooling, with docs/roadmap.md and STATUS promoted In Progress -> Alpha in the same commit.
v2_0_targets: csam-shield: Operator playbook — latency budgets, review-queue operations, audit-log retention, incident handling, and a compatibility matrix across supported Node/Python and major framework versions — plus multi-provider ensemble config (Arachnid + PDQ + Cloudflare) behind the strategy selector with documented coverage gaps (image vs video).

csam-shield: Hardened audit trail on the shared portfolio audit-log format (signed/append-only), rate limiting/quota controls, metrics/observability exports, and a reference end-to-end integration with the Legal/Ops reporting track (operator-configured CyberTipline hand-off) gated on counsel-reviewed docs.

promptshield: Defense-in-depth + observability — decision metrics, block-rate dashboards, false-allow alerting, classifier drift monitoring, multilingual lexicon packs with governed/auditable updates, and a documented evaluation harness so operators can re-benchmark on their own traffic; policy remains tunable-but-bounded (cannot be configured below a safe-minimum deny threshold).

promptshield: Operator deployment guide covering the FastAPI sidecar Docker image, threshold governance, jurisdiction-aware lexicon profiles (minor-indicator definitions vary by country/art convention), and red-team/new-jailbreak turnaround process.

c2pa-lite: Full trust-chain + revocation handling, time-stamping authority support, hardware-key (KMS/PKCS#11) signing as first-class, the durable detached-manifest recovery store (axum + S3/Postgres) for post-strip recovery, and a conformance suite proving interop across major C2PA verifiers; published watermark decode-survival numbers if/when the soft-binding layer graduates from experimental.

c2pa-lite: Operator deployment guide covering signing-key lifecycle/rotation, manifest-store data residency, and provenance-at-scale ingestion patterns, shipped as CLI + library + reference Docker image + ComfyUI/diffusers node.

All three: Cross-package operator bundle — shared audit-log schema, shared config conventions, signed release artifacts (Sigstore/cosign via the Release Captain's v2-hardening track), and a single hardened reference deployment showing csam-shield + promptshield + c2pa-lite running inline in one platform team's pipeline, with the v2.0 threat-model/security review checklist completed.
can_ship_no_externals: csam-shield v0.5 dry-run demo with the existing mock/custom detector + detectkit-test synthetic fixtures, JSONL AuditSink, near-match->pending default-deny, and `make demo` exiting 0 — no Arachnid/PhotoDNA/Cloudflare credentials required.

promptshield v0.5 content-free `guard()` + CLI on the already-implemented Stage 1 conjunction matcher, ambiguous->review, bundled prompt-corpus demo — CPU-only, no model download, no external service.
c2pa-lite v0.5 dev-key sign->verify round-trip with the placeholder signing path on a sample image, normalized verify JSON, untrusted labeling — no external CA, KMS, or manifest-store service.

Documentation deliverables across all three: stub-by-default posture, operator-supplied real-provider boundary, explicit non-goals (csam-shield no auto-report; c2pa-lite not a CSAM detector; promptshield one layer not a substitute), and supported manifest/verdict schemas — pure docs, no externals.
The afternoon-adoption acceptance test per package (one-command demo against bundled synthetic fixtures, green `scripts/safety-check.sh`).

promptshield's adversarial jailbreak test-suite scaffold + benign holdout fixtures, and csam-shield's failure-mode tests (timeout/audit-failure/empty-list) — deterministic, content-free, no externals.

cross_track_deps.why: csam-shield's zero-credential in-box detector path is PDQ-via-hashkit; and all three of my packages should use detectkit-test as the shared legally-clean fixture source for their one-command demos rather than minting bespoke fixtures.

cross_track_deps.why: csam-shield AuditSink, promptshield hash-only audit, and c2pa-lite verification records should converge on one auditable format for the v2.0 operator bundle, and v2.0 requires signed artifacts + the security-review checklist owned by this track.

cross_track_deps.needs: The untracked main-checkout package implementations committed or intentionally split into the v1-adoption worktree
cross_track_deps.why: Per pm-council-notes and release-council, the v1-adoption worktree (created from committed HEAD) does NOT contain the current scaffold work; feature work cannot start until that baseline lands or my track diverges from the real code.

cross_track_deps.needs: /tools portfolio entries and quickstart pages linking each package's one-command demo
cross_track_deps.why: Afternoon adoption depends on discoverability — the demo only drives adoption if a platform team can find it from the portfolio surface.

This gates the start of my track.

csam-shield v1.0 real-detector path is operator-supplied and gated on third-party access: Arachnid Shield self-serve key (low friction, obtainable without enterprise contract) is the realistic first integration; PhotoDNA is access-gated with no public backend SDK and Cloudflare is proxy-bound — so a real default detector cannot be bundled, which is exactly why stub-by-default is correct.

csam-shield reporting (v1.0 hand-off, v2.0 reference integration) requires outside counsel review: confirmed-match handling, evidence preservation, and NCMEC CyberTipline submission are legally governed (18 U.S.C. §2258A) and depend on the Legal/Ops track's counsel retainer — engineering cannot finalize them alone.

promptshield Stage 2 (v1.0) is gated on a curated synthetic/red-team eval set built with zero real CSAM; without a proper eval set it is 'a model, not a defense' (per the README risk + roadmap blocker). The Stage 1 dry-run (v0.5) is NOT blocked by this.

c2pa-lite real signing + interop (v1.0/v2.0) depends on the external c2pa-rs library and the stability of the chosen C2PA spec subset, and on availability of c2patool/CAI Verify for conformance; the watermark soft-binding layer stays NotImplemented because the watermark-removal research target is still moving (an external standards/research dependency, not a code task).
order_of_attack: 0. Unblock the repo baseline first: get the untracked csam-shield/promptshield/c2pa-lite scaffold work committed or split into the v1-adoption worktree (Release Captain coordination) so the track builds on the real code, not stale HEAD.

1. promptshield v0.5 first — lowest-dependency, highest-leverage: Stage 1 is already implemented, it needs no image bytes, no keys, and no Foundation dependency. Promote it to a clean content-free dry-run guard()+CLI+demo and use it to set the default-deny (ambiguous->review) and one-command-demo patterns the other two reuse.

2. c2pa-lite v0.5 second — self-contained sign->verify round-trip with the existing placeholder/dev-key path; no external service and no Foundation dependency, so it ships a clean afternoon demo while clearly labeling dev signatures untrusted.

3. csam-shield v0.5 third — most sensitive (CSAM domain, audit logging, fail-safe semantics) and benefits from the demo/audit patterns hardened on the first two; keep it strictly dry-run with the mock detector + detectkit-test fixtures, near-match->pending, no real provider yet.
4. Standardize `make demo` + bundled synthetic fixtures + green safety-check across all three so the afternoon-adoption promise is uniform and CI-verifiable; update STATUS/roadmap as each hits v0.5.

5. Move to v1.0 in the same order, but csam-shield's v1.0 can begin as soon as Foundation (hashkit/hashkit-match) reaches Alpha (its zero-credential PDQ path) — wire the Arachnid free adapter + resilience controls; promptshield v1.0 waits on the synthetic eval set; c2pa-lite v1.0 lands the c2pa-rs upstream path + c2patool interop.

6. v2.0 hardening last, csam-shield last-of-last because its reference reporting + evidence hand-off carries the heaviest legal (counsel) and cross-track (Legal/Ops) dependencies; finish with the shared-audit-format cross-package operator bundle and signed artifacts via the v2-hardening track.

hashstream v0.5: real diff between two locally-ingested snapshots (added/removed/changed entries) so the existing /diff endpoint serves real data, exercised against fixture lists from detectkit-test.

hashstream v0.5: Ed25519-signed local snapshot manifests with an operator-supplied key, plus a verify endpoint returning true/false — signed snapshots even for fake/local providers, per the Track C v1.0 line pulled forward as the v0.5 dry-run guarantee.

hashstream v0.5: NCMEC/IWF/Arachnid sync defined strictly as an interface with a deterministic in-memory fake provider as the default; the credentialed sync adapters stay stubs and are skipped in default CI.

hashstream v0.5: append-only audit-log entries for every ingest, snapshot, and diff (who/what/when, no secrets) written to a local sink, so access logging exists from alpha rather than being bolted on later.

trainguard v0.5: real LAION-format JSON manifest reader (replacing the scaffold stub) that yields image refs, plus end-to-end scan_dataset() over a synthetic manifest against an InMemoryHashListProvider, producing a real ComplianceReport.

trainguard v0.5: HashStream-backed provider wired behind the existing hash-list adapter interface, pointed at a locally-ingested hashstream snapshot, so the trainguard->hashstream dry-run chain works without credentials.

Both: shared signing/provenance fixtures (test keypair) and golden snapshot + golden ComplianceReport fixtures checked in, so the operator-list -> hashstream snapshot -> trainguard report chain is verifiable in secret-free CI.

Both: README dry-run examples + failure-mode tests (zero-provider refusal already in trainguard; add empty/garbled-list and bad-signature cases), and output clearly marked NON-AUTHORITATIVE / dry-run.
v1_0_targets: hashstream v1.0: stable, documented, semver'd public API + TypeScript SDK surface (ingest/snapshots/snapshot/diff/verify) frozen, so csam-shield and trainguard can integrate against a contract that will not break under them.

hashstream v1.0: persistent snapshot store (replacing in-memory) with stable immutable snapshot IDs and idempotent ingest, plus self-hostable Docker image — the operational substrate trainguard's reproducible reports depend on.

hashstream v1.0: credentialed NCMEC/IWF/Arachnid sync adapters implemented behind the v0.5 interface, explicitly config-gated, disabled by default, and skipped in default CI; fake provider remains the test default.

hashstream v1.0: hardened, documented append-only audit log for sensitive list access (who ingested/queried which list/version/when) as an operator-responsibility guarantee, since hash lists are evidence-adjacent.

trainguard v1.0: stable semver'd public API (scan_dataset + providers + report schema) and a documented operator-responsibility note, embeddable by a careful operator in a real pre-training pipeline against an operator-owned hashstream snapshot.

trainguard v1.0: reproducibility contract — a pinned hashstream snapshot ID + pinned scanner version yields a byte-stable signed ComplianceReport for a given dataset version (the certifiable-compliance-artifact promise).
trainguard v1.0: WebDataset reader alongside LAION (both currently stubs) so real-world dataset formats are covered, with documented match semantics (exact vs PDQ-perceptual).

synthesis.executive_summary:
This program ships an open-source CSAM/abuse-detection portfolio across three maturity gates (v0.5 dry-run, v1.0 frozen-API, v2.0 hardened) over four PM tracks: Foundation (hashkit, hashkit-match, detectkit-test), Adoption (csam-shield, promptshield, c2pa-lite), Credentialed Infra (hashstream, trainguard), and Legal/Ops (cybertip-cli, evidencevault). The dominant structural fact is that Foundation owns the critical path: hashkit's real PDQ implementation (hash_from_luma + hash_dihedral_from_luma via the pdqhash crate) is the root of the dependency tree, and every PDQ-dependent path downstream — csam-shield's zero-credential detector, hashstream/trainguard perceptual matching, and detectkit-test's corpus loop — is blocked until it lands and produces byte-stable hashes. The good news is that a large fraction of the portfolio has NO Foundation dependency and can be built fully in parallel from the first hour: promptshield (Stage 1 already implemented, no image bytes, CPU-only), c2pa-lite (self-contained dev-key sign/verify), the entire Legal/Ops dry-run surface (cybertip-cli mock-submit + evidencevault custody ledger), and hashstream/trainguard's exact-hash (MD5/SHA1/SHA256) path. Nothing in v0.5 or v1.0 blocks on externals (NCMEC creds, counsel sign-off, enterprise contracts) — those are deliberately deferred behind interface stubs and explicit off-by-default gates.

There is exactly one true wave-zero gate that every track is implicitly waiting on: the untracked main-checkout scaffold work must be committed or split into the release worktrees before any feature work begins (flagged hard by Adoption and Credentialed Infra; release worktrees were cut from a HEAD that does not contain the current scaffolds). Once that lands, the execution shape is: Wave 1 fans out wide on all zero-dependency work while Foundation drives hashkit PDQ depth-first; Wave 2 closes the Foundation conformance loop (detectkit-test corpus -> hashkit -> CI drift-gate against the ThreatExchange C++ reference) which unblocks every downstream PDQ integration; Wave 3 hits the v1.0 gate (native-vs-WASM byte-identical reproducibility, semver API freeze, registry publication) with downstream consumers signing off on frozen contracts before they harden; Wave 4 is v2.0 hardening (real MIH, signed artifacts, multi-tenant/persistence, counsel-gated live paths). Cross-track needs are resolved as written handoffs into docs/ops/handoffs/, never as cross-worktree edits — each track stays inside its own packages and the Release Captain owns integration.

The Release Captain must decide split-by-ownership vs single-commit-then-branch and execute it as Wave 0 — no PM can start cleanly until this is resolved.

hashstream public API/SDK freeze gating (Credentialed Infra vs Adoption): Credentialed Infra wants to freeze the hashstream ingest/snapshot/diff/verify contract at v1.0; Adoption insists csam-shield (real-time middleware) AND trainguard (batch) must both sign off on the snapshot/match shape BEFORE freeze or one consumer will be unable to use it. The Release Captain must adjudicate whether the schema-now/impl-later compromise is acceptable to Legal/Ops.

synthesis.recommendation_for_agents: Fan-out model: assign one agent per package, with hashkit getting the strongest agent because it is the solo critical path and everything PDQ-dependent waits on it. Hard rules for every agent: (1) Stay inside your own package directory and your assigned worktree/branch — NEVER edit another track's files. Cross-track needs are written to docs/ops/handoffs/<track>.md as a request, and the Release Captain integrates. This is principle 4 (deps -> handoffs, not edits). (2) Do NOT block on externals — NCMEC/IWF/Arachnid credentials, outside counsel sign-off, ESP agreements, PhotoDNA/Cloudflare access, and enterprise contracts are ALL out of scope for this session. Anything that needs them ships as an interface stub with a deterministic in-memory fake default, or as an explicitly off-by-default/inert gate (e.g. cybertip-cli --live, hashstream credentialed adapters, csam-shield NCMEC reporter). The package must be fully exercisable and publishable with zero credentials. (3) Synthetic fixtures only — no real CSAM hashes, no real credentials; pull test inputs from detectkit-test, not bespoke fixtures; pass bash scripts/safety-check.sh before every push. (4) Default-deny safety bias everywhere: uncertain/near-match -> review/pending, never auto-block or auto-report; label all dry-run output NON-AUTHORITATIVE. Sequencing discipline: do Wave 0 (repo baseline) before anything; in Wave 1 the four satellite/infra streams (promptshield, c2pa-lite, cybertip-cli, evidencevault) and the two exact-hash infra packages (hashstream, trainguard) run fully parallel and do NOT wait for Foundation — only the corpus loop, hashkit-match, csam-shield's PDQ path, and hashstream/trainguard's perceptual path wait. Within Adoption, build promptshield FIRST to set the default-deny + one-command-demo patterns, then reuse them in c2pa-lite and csam-shield; build csam-shield LAST of the three (most safety-sensitive). Within Legal/Ops, build evidencevault (custody backbone) before cybertip-cli. Hard barrier at v1.0: Foundation must freeze the PDQ/match/on-disk-encoding APIs under semver and downstream consumers (csam-shield, trainguard) must sign off on the contract BEFORE freeze — record sign-off in handoffs. Defer real MIH, signed artifacts, multi-tenant/persistence, and all counsel-gated live paths to v2.0. When you finish a wave, update your package STATUS line and docs/roadmap.md in the same commit so the roadmap never drifts from reality.
